lessons.title: Use CTEs
lessons.summary: Break complex queries into named steps.
lessons.explanation: WITH creates temporary named result sets that can be referenced by the final SELECT.
lessons.example:
WITH revenue_by_order AS (
  SELECT order_id, SUM(quantity * unit_price) AS revenue
  FROM sales
  GROUP BY order_id
)
SELECT o.id, c.name, r.revenue
FROM revenue_by_order r
JOIN orders o ON o.id = r.order_id
JOIN customers c ON c.id = o.customer_id;

exercises.prompt: Find paid orders with revenue over 1000. Return columns: id, name, revenue. Order by: o.id ASC.
exercises.expectedSql: WITH revenue_by_order AS (SELECT order_id, SUM(quantity * unit_price) AS revenue FROM sales GROUP BY order_id) SELECT o.id, c.name, r.revenue FROM revenue_by_order r JOIN orders o ON o.id = r.order_id JOIN customers c ON c.id = o.customer_id WHERE o.status = 'paid' AND r.revenue > 1000 ORDER BY o.id;

exercises.prompt: Use a CTE to find departments with an average salary above 85000. Return columns: name, average_salary. Order by: name ASC.
exercises.expectedSql: WITH department_salary AS (SELECT d.name, AVG(e.salary) AS average_salary FROM employees e JOIN departments d ON d.id = e.department_id GROUP BY d.name) SELECT name, average_salary FROM department_salary WHERE average_salary > 85000 ORDER BY name;

exercises.prompt: Use a CTE to calculate project workload and show projects over 40 hours per week. Return columns: name, total_hours. Order by: name ASC.
exercises.expectedSql: WITH project_hours AS (SELECT p.name, SUM(ep.hours_per_week) AS total_hours FROM employee_projects ep JOIN projects p ON p.id = ep.project_id GROUP BY p.name) SELECT name, total_hours FROM project_hours WHERE total_hours > 40 ORDER BY name;

exercises.prompt: Use a CTE to show each customer's total paid revenue. Return columns: name, revenue. Order by: c.name ASC.
exercises.expectedSql: WITH paid_revenue AS (SELECT o.customer_id, SUM(s.quantity * s.unit_price) AS revenue FROM orders o JOIN sales s ON s.order_id = o.id WHERE o.status = 'paid' GROUP BY o.customer_id) SELECT c.name, p.revenue FROM paid_revenue p JOIN customers c ON c.id = p.customer_id ORDER BY c.name;

exercises.prompt: Use a CTE to find employees assigned to more than one project. Return columns: first_name, last_name, project_count. Order by: e.id ASC.
exercises.expectedSql: WITH assignment_counts AS (SELECT employee_id, COUNT(*) AS project_count FROM employee_projects GROUP BY employee_id) SELECT e.first_name, e.last_name, a.project_count FROM assignment_counts a JOIN employees e ON e.id = a.employee_id WHERE a.project_count > 1 ORDER BY e.id;

lessons.title: Use Subqueries
lessons.explanation: A subquery can calculate a value or list of values that the outer query uses for filtering.

exercises.prompt: Find employees whose salary is above the company average. Return columns: first_name, last_name, salary. Order by: id ASC.
exercises.expectedSql: SELECT first_name, last_name, salary FROM employees WHERE salary > (SELECT AVG(salary) FROM employees) ORDER BY id;

exercises.prompt: Find projects with a budget above the average project budget. Return columns: name, budget. Order by: id ASC.
exercises.expectedSql: SELECT name, budget FROM projects WHERE budget > (SELECT AVG(budget) FROM projects) ORDER BY id;

exercises.prompt: Find customers who have placed at least one paid order. Return columns: name, city. Order by: id ASC.
exercises.expectedSql: SELECT name, city FROM customers WHERE id IN (SELECT customer_id FROM orders WHERE status = 'paid') ORDER BY id;

exercises.prompt: Find products whose unit price is above the average unit price. Return columns: product, unit_price. Order by: id ASC.
exercises.expectedSql: SELECT product, unit_price FROM sales WHERE unit_price > (SELECT AVG(unit_price) FROM sales) ORDER BY id;

exercises.prompt: Find employees who are assigned to any project. Return columns: first_name, last_name. Order by: id ASC.
exercises.expectedSql: SELECT first_name, last_name FROM employees WHERE id IN (SELECT employee_id FROM employee_projects) ORDER BY id;

lessons.title: Window Functions
lessons.summary: Calculate values across related rows without collapsing them.
lessons.explanation: Window functions use OVER to calculate rankings, totals, and comparisons while keeping row-level detail.

exercises.prompt: Rank employees by salary from highest to lowest. Return columns: first_name, last_name, salary, salary_rank. Order by: salary_rank ASC, id ASC.
exercises.expectedSql: SELECT first_name, last_name, salary, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY salary DESC) AS salary_rank FROM employees ORDER BY salary_rank, id;

exercises.prompt: Show each employee with the average salary of their department. Return columns: first_name, last_name, department_id, salary, department_average. Order by: id ASC.
exercises.expectedSql: SELECT first_name, last_name, department_id, salary, AVG(salary) OVER (PARTITION BY department_id) AS department_average FROM employees ORDER BY id;

exercises.prompt: Number orders from oldest to newest. Return columns: id, order_date, status, order_number. Order by: order_number ASC.
exercises.expectedSql: SELECT id, order_date, status, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY order_date ASC) AS order_number FROM orders ORDER BY order_number;

exercises.prompt: Show each sale with total revenue for its category. Return columns: product, category, line_revenue, category_revenue. Order by: id ASC.
exercises.expectedSql: SELECT product, category, quantity * unit_price AS line_revenue, SUM(quantity * unit_price) OVER (PARTITION BY category) AS category_revenue FROM sales ORDER BY id;

exercises.prompt: Rank projects by budget from largest to smallest. Return columns: name, budget, budget_rank. Order by: budget_rank ASC, id ASC.
exercises.expectedSql: SELECT name, budget, DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY budget DESC) AS budget_rank FROM projects ORDER BY budget_rank, id;
